name: Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF): Fostering Scheme
coverage: All of Singapore (the national Fostering Scheme, for children under 18)
notes: Couples apply through SG Cares, the government volunteer portal, with a Singpass login. The main applicant and the spouse each make an SG Cares account. MSF's user guide (October 2026 version, read) lists what the profile asks: personal details, marital status, religion, highest education, employment, household members, and the co-applicant's annual income. The form itself was not opened: volunteer.gov.sg refused our reader's robots.txt request (HTTP 403). The form address is the 'Register here' link on Boys' Town's fostering page. MSF also lists a hotline and an email address for its fostering division, and links an online eligibility checker. Its events page lists information sessions run by the fostering agencies. Assessment is by MSF or an MSF-appointed agency and takes about three months. Checked 2026-11-25.

name: MSFCare Network: Fostering Scheme (information page)
coverage: All of Singapore (information only; signposts to the MSF Fostering Scheme)
notes: MSF's volunteering page describes fostering as a volunteer role for couples. Its 'Register your interest' link goes to MSF's 'Apply to be a foster parent' guide (see sg-sg-msf-fostering-scheme). It also links a starter kit for families. No form on the page. Checked 2026-11-25.

name: Ask.gov.sg: MSF answers on fostering and adoption (information site)
coverage: All of Singapore (information only; signposts to MSF's fostering and adoption pages)
notes: Question-and-answer pages for MSF on a shared government platform. In November 2026 the 'Fostering Service' topic held 26 answers, and 'Adoption Services' held answers on procedures and costs. A 'Contact us' link leads to a question form; the site's robots.txt asks readers not to fetch that path, so it was not opened. Checked 2026-11-25.

name: Boys' Town Fostering Services
coverage: All of Singapore (areas served not stated); also supports children in kinship care
stated_response_time: Once the enquiry is submitted, our staff will get in touch with you within 3 working days.
notes: Appointed by MSF in February 2015 as one of the first two pilot fostering agencies; began work in November 2015. The enquiry form on the page asks for name, contact number, email and a short description, and asks people not to give sensitive details before staff follow up. Formal applications go through MSF's SG Cares form, naming Boys' Town as the supporting agency. Listed on MSF's 'Our Fostering Agencies' page with an email address and a mobile number. MSF's events page lists a Boys' Town information session on Saturday 28 November. An older volunteer page on the same site (dated 2023) still lists the income and education criteria that MSF removed in July 2024. Fostering page dated 15 October 2026. Checked 2026-11-25.

name: Epworth Foster Care (Epworth Community Services)
coverage: All of Singapore (areas served not stated)

MSF's events page (read) lists an Epworth information session on Saturday 12 December. Checked 2026-11-25.

name: Gracehaven Fostering (The Salvation Army)
coverage: All of Singapore (areas served not stated)
notes: salvationarmy.org.sg refused our reader (HTTP 403, including robots.txt), so the page was seen only in search results. MSF's 'Our Fostering Agencies' page (read) lists it with an email address and a mobile number. An MSF release (2019) says The Salvation Army was appointed between 2015 and 2017. Checked 2026-11-25.

name: PPIS Oasis (Persatuan Pemudi Islam Singapura)
coverage: All of Singapore (areas served not stated)
notes: The third fostering agency appointed by MSF, set up in 2017. The 'Oasis Fostering Interest Form' asks for name, email, contact number, date of birth, marital status, occupation, what the person wants to know about, how they heard of PPIS, a short enquiry (up to 180 characters) and consent. No reply time is stated. The page says applicants go through a series of interviews and the process takes up to 3 months. The address ppis.sg/oasis/ redirects here. Listed on MSF's 'Our Fostering Agencies' page with an email address and a mobile number. MSF's events page lists an online PPIS Oasis session on Friday 15 January. Page dated 19 October 2026. Checked 2026-11-25.

name: Projek Sinar Ihsan (Muhammadiyah Association)
coverage: All of Singapore (areas served not stated)

name: Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF): Adoption
coverage: All of Singapore (local and foreign children; MSF also acts as Guardian-in-Adoption in court cases)
notes: The 'MSF Adoption Enquiry' form (FormSG; MSF's short link go.gov.sg/adoptionenquiries) has 30 fields. It asks for name, identity number, citizenship and pass type, mobile number and email, and what help is needed (adopting a child, ASA matters, Dependant's Pass, Guardian-in-Adoption, searching for birth parents, other). It asks about joint or sole application and marital status, and has yes or no questions on residence, residency status, age (at least 25, and 21 years older than the child), marriage recognition, spouse consent and serious convictions. It also asks who is being adopted, whether the child is local or foreign, and has an optional document upload. The form says an acknowledgement receipt is emailed; no reply time is stated. Read from the form's public definition, the same data the page loads; nothing was submitted. Prospective adopters start with mandatory briefings at an Authorised Adoption Agency (see the agency rows). MSF also lists a hotline and links an online eligibility checker. Checked 2026-11-25.

name: TOUCH Adoption (TOUCH Community Services)
coverage: All of Singapore; also consultations on adopting related children from China
notes: Authorised Adoption Agency (AAA) on MSF's adoption contact page; says it was the first authorised adoption agency in Singapore. Prospective adopters start with a Pre-Adoption Briefing: TOUCH asks for registration requests by email, and MSF's briefings page links a booking page for TOUCH sessions. The 'Contact Us For An Appointment' form (form_url) was not opened. Also runs ASAs, disclosure briefings, child placement services and China-related adoption consultations. Published fees include a group briefing at $81.75 and an ASA at $2,180 (unrelated or relative child) or $1,199 (biological or stepchild), all with GST. Checked 2026-11-25.

name: Fei Yue Community Services: Adoption
coverage: All of Singapore; also adoptions of related children from China
notes: Authorised Adoption Agency on MSF's adoption contact page; adoption service since April 2002. Group Pre-Adoption Briefings run on weekdays by Zoom in English or Mandarin, at $81.75 a person including GST; registration goes through MSF's booking links. ASA fees are $1,199 (related child) or $2,180 (unrelated child) including GST, plus a non-refundable $261.60 service fee from 1 October 2025. Centre visits are by appointment; the centre page gives an email address and a WhatsApp number. The general contact form (name, contact number, email, purpose, message) does not list adoption as a purpose. Checked 2026-11-25.

name: Lutheran Community Care Services (LCCS): Parenting and Adoption Services
notes: Authorised Adoption Agency for briefings (English only) and ASAs. Briefing registration goes through MSF's booking links; ASA enquiries by email or phone. Fees (GST exempt): briefings $75 a person or $150 a couple from May 2026; ASA $1,100 (biological or stepchild) or $2,000 (relative or unrelated child); extension $150 with no material changes. Also offers prescreening for single applicants and for couples married under 3 years. Page dated 11 November 2026. Checked 2026-11-25.

name: APKIM Centre for Social Services (ACOSS): Adoption Services
coverage: All of Singapore; places Muslim children with Muslim families only
notes: Authorised Adoption Agency on MSF's adoption contact page. The page says all prospective adopters must attend a Pre-Adoption Briefing first, booked through MSF's links. It offers one-to-one consultations by appointment at $160 a session, but also says adoption officers will not respond to emails, calls or drop-ins on adoption matters. Muslim couples with a favourable ASA can ask to join a waiting list for a match. Fees: briefings $75 a person; ASA $1,100 or $2,000; matching $3,000; free for birth families. Checked 2026-11-25.
